text: Dry brining is what I prefer which is basically rubbing the bird with salt and about 1% of the actual weight of the chicken and then left in the fridge for up to 48 hours. The salt draws a little moisture out of the skin and that moisture then disolves the salt and that saltly liquid diffuses back into the meat which results in the proteins in chicken holding more water during cooking. The flavor is better because there's no dilution by adding water and crispier skin.
